steps.name: Implement WrappedText.wrappedLines greedy word-wrap
steps.criteria: Replace the scaffold stub in WrappedText.wrappedLines(measurer:maxWidth:) with a real greedy word-wrap algorithm. Words are split on whitespace. Words are added to the current line until adding the next word would cause the measured line width to exceed maxWidth; at that point the current line is committed and a new line begins. Measurement uses measurer?(word, fontSize)?.width ?? (fontSize * Float(word.count)). Empty content returns an empty array. A single word wider than maxWidth is placed on its own line without infinite looping. The method is pure and has no side effects.
steps.scenario_name: WrappedText is accepted by LayoutEngine as a View and returns a LayoutTree

steps.name: Implement layoutWrappedTextNode branch in LayoutEngine
steps.criteria: Add a layoutWrappedTextNode branch inside LayoutEngine.layoutNode() that matches on WrappedText before the ContainerView fallback. The branch calls wrappedLines(measurer:maxWidth:) with the injected textMeasurer and constraints.maxWidth to obtain the line strings. For each line at index i a child LayoutNode is created with frame origin (x: 0, y: Float(i) * fontSize), size (width: measured line width, height: fontSize). The root LayoutNode frame is width = constraints.maxWidth, height = Float(lineCount) * fontSize. Scenario coverage for this step (scenarios that turn GREEN after both steps complete): (2) multi-line item description produces two or more child nodes; (3) no child LayoutNode frame width exceeds constraints maxWidth; (4) child nodes are stacked vertically with y-origins at multiples of fontSize; (5) root node height equals total line count times lineHeight; (6) root node frame width equals constraints maxWidth; (7) single short text that fits on one line produces exactly one child node; (8) single-line child frame width does not exceed maxWidth; (9) identical inputs always produce identical LayoutTrees; (10) text that exactly fills one line produces exactly one child without overflow; (11) WrappedText color and fontSize are accessible after construction. All 11 Slice 1 acceptance tests pass when both steps are complete.
